evidence.claim: SIF (Specialized Investment Fund) introduced under SEBI Mutual Funds Regulations 2026, effective 1 April 2026; min ₹10 lakh per PAN within a single AMC's SIF offerings (aggregate, not per-scheme); SIP/STP allowed; breach of threshold freezes units (30 days to rebalance if investor-initiated); MF Lite is the passive-only sibling framework.
evidence.source_title: SIF vs Mutual Funds vs PMS vs AIF: Where SEBI's New 2026 Category Fits
evidence.quote: The Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) is a new investment category introduced by SEBI under the Mutual Funds Regulations 2026 (effective 1 April 2026)... minimum investment of ₹10 lakh per investor per fund house... sits between mutual funds and the more exclusive worlds of PMS and AIF

evidence.claim: SIF strategy categories include Equity Long-Short (market-neutral) and Debt Long-Short (interest-rate) funds; naked shorts up to 25% + hedging; expense ratio capped ~2.25%/2%; taxed like mutual funds (Section 10(23D) fund-level nil)
evidence.source_title: SIF Full Form, SEBI India Guide 2026
evidence.quote: Equity Long Short Fund... Position Mix 75% Long 25% Short... Expense Ratio Max 2.25% & 2%... Similar to Mutual Funds, depending on asset class

evidence.claim: PFRDA amended NPS Exits & Withdrawals Regulations effective 16 Dec 2025: non-government subscribers lose 5-year lock-in; lump-sum exit raised to 80% (was 60%), annuity minimum 20% (was 40%); deferment age extended 75 to 85; 100% withdrawal threshold raised to ₹8 lakh (was ₹5 lakh); partial withdrawals allowed up to 4 times before 60, 3 after; loans against corpus allowed; banks permitted to set up pension funds
evidence.source_title: NPS Withdrawal Rules 2026 (secondary summary of PFRDA Gazette 16.12.2025)
evidence.quote: non-government subscribers can now withdraw up to 80% lump sum (was 60%) with minimum 20% annuity (was 40%); deferment age extended to 85 (was 75); small corpus threshold raised to 8 lakh for 100% withdrawal (was 5 lakh)

evidence.claim: FY 2026-27 (AY 2027-28) slabs unchanged from Budget 2025 reset: new regime 0 up to ₹4L, 5% 4-8L, 10% 8-12L, 15% 12-16L, 20% 16-20L, 25% 20-24L, 30% above; 87A rebate ₹60,000 (₹12L tax-free; ₹12.75L salaried with ₹75k std deduction); old regime slabs also unchanged
evidence.source_title: New Income Tax Slab Rates in Budget 2026
evidence.quote: Union Budget 2026 has not made any changes to the income tax slab rates... The new tax regime under Section 115BAC continues to apply with the revised slab rates introduced [in Budget 2025]

evidence.claim: RBI MPC (3-5 Aug 2026) held repo at 5.25%, SDF 5.00%, MSF/Bank Rate 5.50%, stance neutral, 4th consecutive hold; GDP projected 6.7% for FY2026-27
evidence.quote: Governor Shri Sanjay Malhotra announced the MPC's decision on August 5, 2026... to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent, the SDF rate at 5.00 per cent and the MSF rate and Bank Rate at 5.50 per cent, with the stance retained at neutral

evidence.claim: Small savings rates unchanged 8 consecutive quarters incl. Q1 FY 2026-27 (Apr-Jun 2026): SCSS 8.2%, PPF 7.1%, MIS 7.4%, NSC 7.7%
evidence.source_title: Small Savings Schemes Interest Rates Unchanged For April-June 2026 (Outlook Money)
evidence.quote: the government kept the small savings interest rate unchanged for eight consecutive quarters. The Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS) offers the highest interest rate of 8.2 per cent annually. PPF stays at 7.1 per cent

evidence.claim: LRS limit remains USD 250,000/person/FY; Budget 2025 revised TCS thresholds (education from own funds: ₹10L threshold; foreign tour: ₹10L; medical: above ₹5L etc.)
evidence.quote: Before Budget 2025-26, the annual limit under LRS was ₹2.5 lakh (USD 250,000)... the overall annual limit of USD 250,000 per individual remains the same, but the TCS thresholds and slabs have changed
